requirements.statement: Authenticate before displaying any team member, score, exam or chart data.
Exactly one role per user: Administrator, Assessor, Team Member, Viewer.
Only an Administrator may create, modify or deactivate accounts and role assignments.
A Team Member may not view another individual's scores except as part of a radar chart for a team they belong to.
An Assessor may record scores only for assigned teams.
A Viewer may not create or modify any record.
Refusals must not disclose the withheld data.
Scores are integers 1-10; invalid scores are rejected, not coerced.
A Team Member may attempt only an assigned exam.
Exam scoring and 1-10 band conversion are computed from the stored answer key.
3-12 skill axes, at least 6 members, limits reported when exceeded.
Bulk import validates per row and reports rejections with reasons.
A team member exports their own complete record.
Administrator deletion removes a member and their scores from every surface.
Audit entry for every score create, change or delete, Administrator-retrievable.
Answer keys are never retrievable by a Team Member or Viewer.
WCAG 2.2 AA; chart series distinguishable without color; keyboard operable.
Ten fake users for build-step testing must be synthetic.

conflicts.name: Regulatory scope self-contradictory
sources: security notes: GDPR and CCPA apply

conflicts.name: Radar chart contradicts Team Member confidentiality
conflicts.detail: FR-7.3 requires per-member attribution and FR-6.2 requires the same data as a table from one dataset (DR-7), so the chart is not an aggregate. The FR-1.4 carve-out becomes the general case and the peer confidentiality boundary is undefined.

conflicts.name: Session transport undecided leaves CSRF posture undecided
Self-assessment can raise a member's own charted score
conflicts.detail: Read literally the specification lets a Team Member set their own displayed skill level; FR-5.11 requires the method be distinguishable only in the score detail view, not on the chart.

conflicts.name: Answer-key confidentiality does not prevent collusion

documentationGaps: No API specification (OpenAPI/GraphQL/protobuf) — entry points derived from requirements only
No data model or schema — field sensitivity inferred
No authorization matrix — the central control exists only as prose
No architecture diagram — stage 08 diagrams are synthesized, not absorbed
No prior threat model to diff against
No cloud provider, CI system or runtime topology (SQ-8)
No chart rendering library decision, deferring the most XSS-relevant DEP-* review
assumptions: All documents are current: none is dated, all were modified on the same day as the latest commits.
SECURITY.md's CONFIRMED/PROVISIONAL labels describe provenance, not implementation status; all 48 rules are recorded as Claimed — Not Verified.
The security notes referenced by SECURITY.md are not present in the repository; their content is known only through SECURITY.md's restatement of it.
